source.title: Understanding the geometry of deep learning with decision boundary volume
source.authors: M. Burfitt; Jacek Brodzki; Paweł Dłotko

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; minor apparent transcription/typo issues, but no material cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies dropout and measures test accuracy together with decision-boundary volume measures, testing whether a measured network property tracks generalization. It does not test the broader memorization, optimizer, batch-size, architecture-comparison, or sharpness claims.
record.gate_note: The eligible results are the dropout sweeps reporting test accuracy and TrainBvol/LAdvBvol for each dataset, architecture, and optimizer. Bvol measurements are explicitly omitted from the main experiments because they provided less information due to measurement noise. Results cited from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study varies dropout, includes zero-dropout controls, and reports held-out classification accuracy, directly testing V6 with the same intervention and outcome. Its decision-boundary measures do not test V7. The study is not an original source for V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record largely captures the authors' conclusion: boundary-volume critical points often accompany better generalization, with convolutional optima around TrainBvol minima and more variable relationships for fully connected networks. The detailed results qualify exact coincidence: some convolutional minima precede the accuracy optimum. These are proof-of-concept associations, not evidence that boundary volume causes generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures decision-boundary neighborhood volumes while varying dropout; it does not test the original V6 dropout comparisons or the stated small-data and joint-regularization conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported relationship varies by architecture, dataset, optimizer, and dropout rate. The authors also note measurement noise in Bvol and curvature effects on TrainBvol for MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Convolutional accuracy optima occur around or shortly after TrainBvol minima; fully connected accuracy optima correspond to dataset- and optimizer-dependent critical points in TrainBvol or LAdvBvol.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-space decision-boundary neighborhood volumes can correlate with held-out accuracy across dropout settings. These quantities differ from magnitude-aware weight-space sharpness.

record.problems: The authors describe the experiments as proof of concept and report only plotted means and one standard deviation, without exact values in the prose. Results are based on 10 random initializations. Bvol results were omitted from the main dropout experiments because of measurement noise. The method uses FGSM and acknowledges its effectiveness limitations, especially away from training data.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows omitted. Bvol measurements are explicitly omitted by the paper from the main dropout experiments because they provided less information due to measurement noise (Section 7.4).

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width changes beyond the interpolation threshold.

Comparative convolutional versus fully connected test error, the contribution of locality, and convolution-derived initialization. Architecture-dependent boundary-volume patterns do not establish these comparisons.

Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer generalization under comparable tuning budgets. Separate MNIST sweeps use different learning rates and training durations without a reported comparative performance conclusion.
Batch-size effects and recipe adaptations; batch size is fixed at 32.

Very small training sets; demonstrated underfitting from excessive dropout; joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. Most sweeps also do not isolate dropout from training-duration changes.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus matched random removals.

missing.what: Recover held-out accuracy at zero and positive dropout, with uncertainty, for fully connected Fashion MNIST and CIFAR-10. The recorded geometric trends and local peaks do not establish whether dropout improves accuracy over baseline; the supplied text contains no readable plot values.
missing.locator: Figure 10, third and fourth rows, test-accuracy panels

record.verdict_notes: The blanket limits_scope verdict is unwarranted: V6 already allows regime dependence and suitably configured dropout. Plateaus, noisy peaks and untested clauses do not themselves limit that claim. Exact accuracy gains and their statistical significance cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Comparison of convolutional and fully connected generalization or learned local connectivity.
Comparative adaptive-optimizer generalization under tuning regimes.

Dropout effects on held-out accuracy are tested in several architecture, dataset, and optimizer settings. Small training sets, too much dropout causing underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
